title: News 10.28.2026
content: Biological mechanism underlying Huntington’s disease may be more widespread in the brain than previously thought Findings suggest new drugs under development could potentially protect multiple parts of the brain. By Leah Eisenstadt October 28, 2026 Credit: Courtesy of the McCarroll lab A new study revealed that aggregations of the huntingtin protein (pink) occur within nuclei (blue) of cells with highly expanded DNA repeats in both the striatum and neocortex of individuals with Huntington's disease.
